Detailed knowledge of key systems — AI tools, SAP, and Excel required
Strong project-management and organizational skills with the ability to meet tight deadlines consistently
Deep knowledge of the local country tax system
Strong negotiation skills
Fully bilingual in English and Spanish
Preferred qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, or a related field
CPA, MBA, or equivalent professional qualification

title: Security Engineer - Developer Experience
description:
The Apple Services Engineering Security team builds and provides secure systems and infrastructure that fuel Apple's services, including iCloud, Music, Siri, and the App Store. As part of the ASE Security team, you will help manage the security needs of Apple’s services around the world.
We're looking for a Developer Experience Security Engineer to help engineers across Apple build secure software with confidence, closing the gap between security guidance and engineering practice by crafting the documentation, automation, and learning resources that make secure development intuitive, accessible, and frictionless at scale.
As a Developer Experience Security Engineer on the Services Engineering Security team, you will own the creation and maintenance of the resources that application, infrastructure, and platform engineers depend on to build securely. This is a highly collaborative cross-functional role that blends software development, technical writing, and strategic communication to drive measurable adoption of security practices across Apple's engineering community.
You will be the connective tissue between security standards and the engineers who implement them across the software development lifecycle; translating complex technical requirements into clear, actionable guidance and helping teams adopt new practices, onboard to tooling, integrate security frameworks, and stay aligned as standards evolve.
Minimum qualifications: 7+ years of experience in a software engineering, developer experience, or technical writing role with an understanding of software build, deploy, and monitoring principles, including software supply chain engineering and SDLC practices
Demonstrated ability to write production-quality automation, including Slack workflows and integrations, and tooling for issue and ticket lifecycle management
Familiarity with LLM-assisted development tools and experience writing prompt instructions, skills files, or system prompts that shape model behavior for specific domains
Proven ability to distill complex technical topics into clear, precise writing and reference documentation for engineering audiences, including FAQs, how-to guides, and onboarding materials
Proven ability to work cross-functionally, designing and executing campaigns partnering with engineering teams across diverse organizations to drive behavior
Self-directed and comfortable making prioritization decisions, and managing multiple workstreams simultaneously
Collaborative team player with strong listening skills, empathy, and a commitment to bringing out the best in peers
Preferred qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related technical field, or equivalent work experience
Familiarity with application security principles, secure coding practices, software supply chain security, or developer-facing security tooling
A portfolio or examples of technical documentation, automation scripts, or LLM skills files is welcome

title: Security Researcher – Red Team
description:
Help Apple secure the world’s most advanced consumer devices, which people trust to store their personal and professional data. We believe that the best defense is a good offense, and that means finding vulnerabilities before attackers do. We're looking for talented and inspired individuals to join our team and attack Apple's products with the goal of better safeguarding our users.
We are looking for a Senior Security Researcher to join our specialized Red Team. In this role, you will focus on the complex boundary where hardware meets software. You will hunt for vulnerabilities in the microarchitecture, memory management, and execution pipelines of modern CPUs and GPUs, as well as in the low-level code which runs on it. If you enjoy bridging the gap between hardware primitives and kernel-level exploits, and have a passion for uncovering side-channels or architectural logic flaws, this is the team for you.
Minimum qualifications: BS in Computer Engineering or related engineering degree.
Experience with modern CPU architectures; such as pipeline stages, caching mechanisms, MMU, or speculative execution.
Experience with low-level software; such as in C, C++, or Assembly.
Experience in discovering vulnerabilities or developing exploits at the OS/Hypervisor level, or in hardware-software interfaces such as CVEs, bug bounties, conference talks, or whitepapers.
Preferred qualifications: 10+ years relevant industry experience.
Extensive familiarity with ARM v8/v9 or x86 instruction sets.
Proven understanding of GPU architectures (execution pipelines, memory hierarchies) and how software interfaces with them (e.g., driver vulnerability research, compute batching, memory isolation).
Deep understanding of operating system internals, kernel architecture, and memory management.
Experience with hardware description languages (Verilog/VHDL) or pre-silicon security validation.
Experience with confidential computing environments.
Familiarity with the security implications of AI/ML hardware accelerators and complex GPU workloads (e.g., memory handling in PagedAttention or Mixture of Experts).
Familiarity with reverse engineering tools (IDA Pro, Ghidra) and dynamic analysis/debugging tools.

title: Senior Human-Centered AI Researcher, Personal Intelligence & Experiences
description:
At Apple, we create intuitive, intelligent experiences that enrich people's lives. We are seeking a Senior Human-Centered AI Researcher to help shape the next generation of software experiences across Apple's ecosystem. In this role, you will lead research that advances our understanding of how people interact with both emerging AI capabilities and established software experiences. Working closely with engineering, design, marketing, data science, and AI/ML modeling teams, you will define research strategies, uncover user needs and expectations, and translate behavioral insights into actionable recommendations that influence product direction, design, quality and ultimately shape the end customer experience.
Our team conducts human-centered research throughout the software and AI-feature development lifecycle, from understanding user needs and expectations to evaluating early prototypes and assessing product experience quality. We combine rigorous qualitative and quantitative methods to understand how people perceive, interact with, and experience software, including intelligent and adaptive systems.
The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in experimental design, statistical analysis, and mixed-methods research, with the scientific judgment to select and adapt methodologies to complex product questions. You will independently lead research initiatives across multiple product areas, collaborating with cross-functional partners to identify critical research questions, establish meaningful evaluation criteria, and translate findings into actionable product recommendations.
This role requires the ability to communicate complex findings to diverse audiences, including senior leadership and executives, and directly influence product strategy and development priorities. You will also contribute to research strategy, advance methodological practices, and mentor other researchers.
Minimum qualifications: PhD in Cognitive Science, Experimental Psychology, Neuroscience, Human-Computer Interaction or a related field with substantial training in quantitative and qualitative research.
5+ years of relevant experience conducting human-centered research in technology or software product development.
Formal training and demonstrated expertise in experimental design, including hypothesis development, study design, sampling strategies, randomization, measurement, and interpretation of experimental results.
Strong proficiency in statistics including t-tests, analysis of variance (ANOVA), regression models, clustering techniques, factor analysis, mixed-effects models, repeated-measures analysis, or other multivariate approaches with the ability to select, apply, and interpret appropriate analyses for complex research questions.
Demonstrated expertise in qualitative and quantitative research methodologies, including survey design, usability testing, Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA), diary studies, field experiments, or other longitudinal and in-situ research programs.
Preferred qualifications: Experience leveraging AI-assisted tools and workflows across the research lifecycle, including but not limited to research design, data processing, qualitative and quantitative analysis, and synthesis of findings, with the ability to critically evaluate AI-generated outputs for accuracy and validity.
Experience researching AI-powered products, generative AI, intelligent systems, or emerging software interaction paradigms.
Experience combining behavioral telemetry, self-reported measures, and qualitative findings to inform product decisions.
Proven ability to translate complex research findings into actionable recommendations and communicate effectively through presentations to senior leadership and executive audiences.
Demonstrated ability to influence product strategy, navigate ambiguous research questions, and provide methodological mentorship to other researchers.

title: Senior Software Developer in Test - Embedded Sensors QE, Core OS
description:
Join the team responsible for ensuring the highest quality for technologies at the heart of products known to surprise and delight our customers.
The Embedded Sensors Quality Engineering team owns and drives the excellence of quality for the Always On Platform (AOP) which enables multiple features - from driving motion sensors like accelerometers, gyroscopes and IMUs to detecting “Hey Siri” and more on all Apple products like the iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods and Apple Vision Pro and more!
This is a highly entrepreneurial team, always looking for innovative ways to improve status quo and solve difficult problems in new and better ways. You will work in a fast paced environment, interacting directly with development teams within the organization as well as cross-functional teams. The nature of the position requires excellent communication skills, strong technical and debugging skills, and a drive to make a difference.
Minimum qualifications: 5+ years of experience with testing or debugging embedded systems or device drivers.
Strong understanding of software test and validation methodologies
Solid OS fundamentals
Programming experience with C/C++, Python and Shell scripting
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Bachelor’s degree in CS/CE/EE (or equivalent, or related field)
Preferred qualifications: Experience with developing, testing or debugging device drivers, firmware, other low level software, embedded systems or sensors

title: Senior Software Engineer, Apple Data Platform
description:
We are looking for software engineers to join our small team with big responsibilities. The role involves a tremendous amount of individual responsibility and influence over the direction of the core service. We believe in small agile teams and their ability to deliver high-quality, high-impact software. We share code ownership and knowledge through the Agile technique of pair-programming. Our codebase is written entirely in modern Rust using the latest technologies and coding practices. We rely on sustainable coding through focus on readable, maintainable, and performant code. As such, we lean heavily on Rust and its great tooling to fearlessly develop highly efficient distributed systems code. We use multiple levels of testing to ensure we have low-level performance (such as tests to validate the number of allocations and bytes used) as well as correctness (such as tests with fault injection, and race condition simulation). Combined with the powerful borrow checker and strong type system of Rust, we can develop complex systems with confidence.
We are building a new distributed multi-tiered data orchestration service to support critical Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning systems and services with direct business and customer value. We are looking for an experienced developer to join our collaborative and friendly team. Someone with a desire to learn. With a passion for clean, maintainable code. Someone that enjoys the duality of working on high level concepts as well as optimizing low-level performance.
All members of the team are responsible for the complete life-cycle of features. This includes identifying areas of improvement, proposing changes, driving implementation, and supporting it in production.
Minimum qualifications: Experience designing, implementing, and supporting highly scalable applications and web services
Experience working with Java or Rust
Experience with concurrent programming (e.g., locking, memory synchronization, atomic operations, etc.)
Experience with distributed system concepts (e.g., distributed consensus, replication, failure detection, etc.)
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science (or related field) or equivalent software development experience
Preferred qualifications: Experience working with Rust (e.g., asynchronous (async/await), sharing models (Sync/Send), etc.)
Experience with blob storage solutions
Experience with distributed key-value databases
Experience with Kubernetes and containers
Experience with Linux system internals
Experience with storage systems and internals
Experience with back-end web technologies

title: Senior Systems Engineer, Watch Software
description:
The watchOS Systems team is looking for a creative senior software engineer to help define the future of Apple Watch. Your core responsibility will be to build and optimize the foundational software that drives the device's performance and power efficiency. You will also have the unique opportunity to conduct investigative research, prototyping new technologies that will help define future hardware and software features. This role is perfect for a collaborative engineer who is passionate about the intersection of hardware and software and thrives on solving complex, open-ended problems.
As a key engineer on this team, you will tackle a wide range of complex challenges and collaborate closely with Performance, Power, OS, and Hardware experts across Apple. Your responsibilities will be dynamic, ranging from architecting core OS features to acting as a performance specialist for other teams. This includes defining and implementing critical system-level functionality, such as new systems to manage the process lifecycle, reclaim memory, or lead the transition to a 64-bit OS architecture. You will also dive into other teams' code to diagnose and resolve significant power issues, and will build and maintain tools to help all engineers model and analyze performance and memory.
Minimum qualifications: 8+ years industry experience.
Deep technical understanding and hands-on experience with software development and lifecycle management.
Experience with low-level OS systems, i.e. kernel, Darwin or drivers.
Deep experience with power and performance measurement and investigation techniques.
Solid computer science fundamentals.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills for collaborating with a technical team.
Preferred qualifications: Experience defining and contributing to application or systems architecture.
Ability to work with technology partners at all levels of the stack, from hardware, sensors, and firmware to frameworks and applications.
Experience in additional technical areas, like Graphics, UI or networking.
Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, especially with ambiguous or undefined problems.

title: Site Reliability Engineer, Apple Data Platform
description:
The Apple Services Engineering team (ASE) is one of the most exciting examples of Apple's long-held passion for combining art and technology. These are the people who power the App Store, Apple TV, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, and Apple Books — at extensive scale, meeting high expectations to deliver a huge variety of entertainment in over 35 languages to more than 150 countries.
Within ASE, the Apple Data Platform SRE team keeps a massive, multi-cloud platform running for thousands of internal engineers building the next generation of data and AI products at Apple. We sit at the intersection of infrastructure, automation, and customer success — running incident response, providing hands-on support to internal teams, and partnering with developers to make cutting-edge services like Spark, Flink, Airflow, Ray, Notebooks and LLM-based agent platforms reliable at scale.
This is a rare opportunity to build deep expertise across one of the most technically diverse platforms at Apple — while specialising in an area that's shaping the future of how Apple builds and operates AI. As an SRE on Apple Data Platform, you'll operate and support the team's full portfolio, from big data pipelines to multi-cloud infrastructure, and grow into the team's go-to expert for ML/AI platform services — including Ray training and serving, LangGraph agent deployments, RAG architectures, embeddings platforms, and vector store platforms. You won't be building the models yourself, but you'll be the infrastructure backbone behind the teams who do — keeping their services, pipelines, and platforms running flawlessly in production so they can focus on innovation.
We're looking for a self-motivated engineer who thrives on ownership — someone who wants a set of services to call their own, the autonomy to drive their reliability roadmap, and the collaborative instinct to keep that work aligned with the team's broader direction. If you love solving hard operational problems, enjoy being the trusted expert customers turn to, and want a front-row seat to Apple's ML/AI infrastructure evolution, this role offers real room to grow your scope and impact over time.
Minimum qualifications: * Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, an engineering-related field, or equivalent related experience.
* 3+ years in a Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, or Infrastructure-focused role.
* Proficient in Python; working knowledge of Golang a plus.
* Experience with Kubernetes and at least one major cloud provider (AWS or GCP).
* Exposure to operating or supporting ML pipelines, model-serving infrastructure, or LLM-based systems in production.
* Strong communication skills and composure under pressure during incidents.
* Solid grounding in SRE principles, with prior on-call or production-support experience.
Preferred qualifications: * Hands-on experience operating or supporting Ray (training/serving), LangGraph or similar agent orchestration frameworks, RAG architectures, embeddings platforms, or vector store platforms.
* Familiarity with MCP-based tooling and ML lifecycle/dataset management systems.
* Experience with S3 and cloud storage/networking fundamentals.
* Familiarity with observability tooling: Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk, PagerDuty.
* Working knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and deployment workflows.
* Deep understanding of one or more Big Data technologies (Spark, Flink, Airflow, Trino, Notebooks).
* A track record of automating manual operations through scripting or tooling.
* Intellectual curiosity and a drive to keep learning — for yourself, your team, and the org.

title: SoC Characterization Product Engineer
description:
Do you love crafting sophisticated solutions to highly complex challenges? Do you intrinsically see the importance in every detail? As part of our Silicon Technologies group, you’ll help design and manufacture our next-generation, high-performance, power-efficient processor, system-on-chip (SoC).
Joining this group means you’ll be responsible for crafting and building the technology that operates Apple’s devices. Together, you and your team will enable our customers to do all the things they love with their devices. We promote innovation and new technology. The people who work here have reinvented and defined entire industries with the Mac, iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, Apple Watch, AirPods, HomePod and a multitude of groundbreaking Accessories. The same passion for innovation that goes into our products also applies to our practices — strengthening our dedication to leave the world better than we found it. In this role, your responsibilities will involve Product Characterization on different setups and defining correlation between ATE and other logic boards. You will also focus on studying the impact of hardware on SOC performance.
If you are ready for a challenge, please apply!
- Perform data analysis, characterization, and fault isolation to resolve root cause of the issues.
- Perform correlation between ATE and different hardware setups.
- Partner with design, process and test engineers to identify and implement corrective actions on both new and mature products and technologies.
- Define and finalize production screening guard-band specifications based upon design intent and characterization result.
- Perform statistical data analysis on mass data set to setup test limits.
- Complete yield analyses and correlation analysis for all levels of test insertions.
- Support test time reduction related characterization activities.
- Coordinate test related activities and reviews with both internal and external groups
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's degree + 3 Years of Experience
Preferred qualifications: In depth knowledge of Semiconductor Manufacturing Process and proven understanding of Electronic Engineering Fundamentals and DFT concepts.
Experience in system level/mother board characterization and data collection.
Expertise in programming with Scripting languages (i.e., PERL, Python)
Knowledgeable with test equipment (i.e., oscilloscope, logic analyzer, etc.)
Board bring up, hardware design and PDN noise analysis experience is a plus.
Excellent interpersonal skills to work with internal team members and external suppliers

description:

title: System Electrical Architect (Input Devices)
description:
Apple is seeking a visionary electrical architect to define and design the future of input devices (trackpads, keyboards, and next-generation interfaces) for our Mac product line. You will be responsible for ground-up (zero-to-one) EE system architecture, transforming open-ended user experience challenges into concrete, innovative hardware solutions. If you are an independent, first-principles thinker who has experience in design for mass production and thrives in ambiguity and is passionate about pushing the boundaries of human-computer interaction, we want you to help us invent what comes next!
In this highly collaborative and impactful role, you will lead the electrical architecture for next-generation input technologies. Input devices sit at the complex intersection of electrical, mechanical, and firmware/software engineering. You will not just be designing circuits. You will be defining the system. Based on design goals, you will propose innovative architectural concepts, drive new technology investigations, and partner with mechanical engineers and firmware engineers to continuously iterate, co-design, and optimize hardware.
Minimum qualifications: BS/MS in Electrical Engineering, or related field with 7+ years of experience in hardware system design or electrical architecture.
Strong EE fundamentals (E&M physics, first principles) with a deep understanding of system architecture and design tradeoffs.
Experience in schematic capture and component selection across diverse domains (power, digital, analog, high-speed, wireless).
Deep knowledge of low-speed and high-speed digital interfaces (e.g., I2C, I2S, SPI, USB, MIPI, PCIe, Thunderbolt).
Experience with highly constrained multilayer PCBs (HDI, fine-pitch BGA) and rigid-flex designs (Allegro preferred).
Hands-on proficiency with advanced lab tools (high-bandwidth oscilloscopes, VNAs, BERT) for bring-up, validation, and protocol decode.
Proven track record of taking complex systems from concept to mass production, collaborating tightly with FW, SW, and ME teams.
Preferred qualifications: Sensing Expertise: High-precision AFE design for weak signals (capacitive touch, strain gauges, piezo).

title: Technical Enablement Engineer

As a Technical Enablement Engineer on the Services Engineering Security team, you will own the creation and maintenance of the resources that application, infrastructure, and platform engineers depend on to build securely. title: Tribologist
description:
Apple's Product Design Materials Engineering team designs and specifies materials used in every Apple product, from metals, glass, and ceramics to composites, polymers, adhesives, and coatings. Every surface that moves, slides, or touches shapes how an Apple product feels and performs, and we're growing our team with a dedicated tribology expert to help define how we design, test, and qualify materials for these interfaces.
We are looking for a senior tribologist to be our team's expert on friction, wear, and lubrication. You will work in our Materials Development Center in Santa Clara, CA. There you'll combine a strong theoretical foundation with practical experimental judgment to shape how Apple designs and qualifies materials for moving interfaces, and to help keep those interfaces working well for customers over years of use.
You will set the technical direction for tribology across Apple's product lines by identifying the friction and wear mechanisms that govern performance and defining test strategies (from coupon-level screening to component-level validation) that match real-world use. You will lead in-depth tribological characterization and failure analysis, working with the lab's broader characterization specialists to identify the wear mechanisms at work and determine root cause. You'll turn these learnings into actionable design choices: material, coating, and lubrication specifications, contact and geometry recommendations, and qualification criteria that product teams can apply with confidence. You will also expand and advance the lab's tribology capability and train and mentor technicians to run routine measurements.
Minimum qualifications: Masters or PhD in Materials Science, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field, with research focused on tribology or surface science
5+ years of industry experience applying tribology to product development, ideally for mechanical components or consumer hardware
Deep expertise in tribology fundamentals, including contact mechanics, friction, and wear mechanisms in metals, ceramics, polymers, and coated surfaces, with the ability to identify wear mechanisms from worn surfaces and failure analysis results
Proven ability to design and interpret coupon-level tribology tests, link the results to component and field performance, and use them to drive material and coating selection
Preferred qualifications: Expertise in surface engineering and coatings for wear-critical interfaces, such as PVD/CVD and DLC coatings, nitriding, anodizing, and other surface treatments, including their effect on scratch and cosmetic wear
Strong knowledge of lubrication, including boundary lubrication, damping greases, solid lubricants, and how lubricants interact with nearby materials
Experience with polymer and elastomer tribology, including self-lubricating polymers, bushings, and seals
Experience working with simulation or modeling teams to turn contact mechanics and wear theory into predictive models
Understanding of tribocorrosion and environmental effects on wear, such as humidity, temperature, and exposure to sweat, skin oils, and cosmetics
Experience designing custom tribology test rigs, including test methods, data handling, and analysis, and building lab capability through equipment specification and internal test standards
A record of mentoring technicians and engineers, communicating clearly with cross-functional partners, and contributing to the field through publications or professional societies such as STLE

title: US Wearables Analytics & Individual AI Lead
description:
The people here at Apple donʼt just build products— they craft the kind of wonder thatʼs revolutionized entire industries. By pairing advanced econometric modeling (such as hedonic price regression) with emerging AI capabilities, you will turn raw market signals into predictive, decision-ready intelligence. Minimum qualifications: 5+ years of hands-on analytical experience in market intelligence, business planning, sales operations, data analytics, or category management within consumer electronics, telecommunications, or retail.
Demonstrated success in consumer/business intelligence, product marketing, product management, commercial management, market research, finance, and strategy planning.
Strong interest in and market familiarity with the wearables ecosystem — smartwatches, health/fitness trackers, adjacent emerging form factors, true wireless audio (TWS), and core accessories.
Ability to connect market share movements, inventory trends, and competitor promotional activity directly to internal run-rates and current-quarter sales pacing.
Demonstrated track record of building automated dashboards and self-serve reporting (Tableau, Power BI, or similar modern BI tools). Experience with Python or R for data wrangling, automation, and data pipeline scripting.
Comfort operating in a fast-moving, high-visibility environment, supporting multiple cross-functional senior stakeholders simultaneously.

Preferred qualifications: Familiarity with or a strong curiosity about applying modern AI/LLM tools to streamline research synthesis and reporting workflows. Experience building custom LLM agents, prompt engineering pipelines, or automated briefing tools (RAG, agent workflows) is highly valued.
Self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced environment, capable of juggling recurring weekly forecasting deadlines with creative, long-term tooling projects.
Expert proficiency in Keynote and Excel, with an eye for clean, minimalist visual design and the ability to translate complex data into concise, easy-to-digest slides.
MBA preferred.

Our goal is to move as many members as possible through the pipeline quickly, while scaling the business without scaling manual work linearly. We have digitized workflows around historically manual, fragmented processes. The next step is making those systems reliable, observable, and safe to operate at scale.

description:

About the Role
In this role, you’ll work within a 5-15k sq ft distribution center, will assist in leading the local warehouse operating team, and in some locations, includes preparing food in a light-prep kitchen, and help the Site Manager ensure we maintain high quality for our customers.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your site, helping your team to navigate new initiatives and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners.
Operate: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results in one or more specific focus areas or a specific shift for your site. Strategize: Within the focus area(s) assigned by your Site Manager, you’ll analyze data and make strategic recommendations and execute actions regarding resource allocation, workflow, warehouse organization and when to engage cross-functional partners. You may also lead some process improvement projects.
Delight: We are customer-obsessed. You’ll coach and empower your team to provide a highly quality customer experience with every order. You’ll also work cross-functionally with central teams from our inventory to training teams to ensure your team has the tools and resources they’ll need to deliver.

You’re a proven leader. You have managed high-performance teams of 5+ employees with successful performance and employee development outcomes.

You solve problems from first principles.   You’re excited to solve problems in innovative ways, and you resist “this is how it’s always been done” thinking.
You’re unafraid of ambiguity.   Rapid change and learning is exciting to you, and you thrive in ambiguous, startup environments.
You’re analytical . You let data win arguments. You are a data-first problem solver and you have experience using Excel or Google Sheets to analyze data, including using basic formulas and creating pivot tables.

title: Studio Central Product Designer
location: San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA; New York, NY
description:
About the Role
At DoorDash we are redefining what it means to be a designer. We are building toward a team of makers, builders, and doers. Between 2005 and 2015, "web designer" became "product designer" and the scope widened. The same shift is happening now, as LLMs expand that scope again, toward strategy on one end and direct execution on the other. As a Staff Visual Designer, you'll practice this build-first way of working with real autonomy: using AI-native tools and code to move from idea to shipped work quickly, and owning craft decisions end to end rather than checking each one against a brief.
You'll join Studio Central, a net-new Product Design team sitting at the intersection of product, brand, and innovation. Studio Central is a global team within Studio, DoorDash's Product Design organization, supporting DoorDash, Wolt, Deliveroo, and 7Rooms. We own how brand shows up in the product experience, partnering closely with Marketing and Product teams to shape cohesive, high-quality work and to help define the foundations, vision, and future state of design across our portfolio. Our work spans major brand moments, merchandising, and the systems that connect it all.
Studio Central's systems and standards are still being built, and everyone building here, regardless of level, has real input into what they become. You'll have full ownership over your own craft and projects, and a real voice in the standards, rituals, and craft bar the whole team ends up working from, not reacting to a framework someone else already finished, but helping shape it as it forms.
We operate in a hybrid working model, 1-2 days out of one of our Design Hubs, the rest working from home.
Your primary impact is craft and output: shipping high-quality, on-brand work across the campaigns, seasonal moments, and merchandising pushes Studio Central owns, with less oversight than earlier-career roles and more responsibility for getting it right yourself. Your secondary impact is revenue, in the same way: the work you ship well, and the craft feedback you give to the designers around you, is part of what raises the expression bar across DoorDash, Wolt, Deliveroo, and 7Rooms as a whole.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will...
Own end-to-end visual craft on brand moments, campaigns, and merchandising pushes, from concept through shipped, production-ready work, with less oversight than earlier-career roles
Mentor other designers as needed, sharing craft feedback and helping them build range, without formal authority over their work
Help build and pressure-test the design systems, component libraries, and AI-powered tooling as a team, whether that's proposing the first version or stress-testing someone else's, and speak up early rather than reacting to a finished one
Practice influencing without authority: bring a strong point of view into rooms with Product, Marketing, and creative stakeholders, and back it up with working prototypes rather than title
Build real range across the full workflow, from rough concept to production-ready execution, and hand off cleanly to engineering so nothing gets lost in translation
We're excited about you because you have...
A portfolio that shows strong, considered visual craft, systems thinking, or brand work at a senior level, even if you haven't yet led an org-wide initiative
Comfort moving between art-direction tools like Figma and Illustrator and shipping in code, or you're closing that gap quickly
A habit of treating a new tool or technique as an experiment worth running, not a decision you need to get right the first time, you'll ship a handful of rough attempts in something you picked up last week before you'd sit through a training on it
Experience giving craft feedback to other designers, even informally, and helping them get sharper
A track record of shipping ambiguous briefs to a high bar without heavy oversight

description:

And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form's Advanced Product Development team is responsible for architecting and designing the next generation of our iron-air battery system — the cell, module, pack, and the support systems that keep them running reliably for decades in the field. We work ahead of our production programs, translating breakthrough electrochemistry and system requirements into electrical, controls, and test systems that can scale to high-volume manufacturing.

We're hiring an Electrical Engineer II to design, build, troubleshoot, and test the control systems and test assets that support development of our next generation of iron-air batteries. As part of our Advanced Product Development team in Somerville, MA, you will spend much of your time in the lab: wiring and commissioning control systems, bringing up new hardware, diagnosing electrical and controls faults, and running system-level tests. You will work with guidance from senior electrical engineers and alongside mechanical and systems engineers and technicians to turn test requirements into safe, reliable, well-documented hardware. This is an exciting opportunity to deliver our sustainable multi-day energy storage solution to the grid!

Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Design, build, wire, and check out control systems for test assets, working from schematics and BOMs through fabrication and documentation.

 - Troubleshoot electrical and controls issues on test assets and prototype hardware, finding root causes with scopes, meters, and data logs and implementing fixes.

 - Bring up and commission new test assets in the lab, including point-to-point checkout, sensor and instrument verification, and functional testing of safety interlocks.

 - Plan and run system-level tests: write test procedures, collect and review data, and report results and issues to the team.

 - Program and modify PLC and HMI logic for test assets with guidance from senior engineers, and keep eCAD schematics, BOMs, and cable/harness documentation current.

 - Partner with mechanical, systems, and test engineers and technicians on tight timelines, and champion lab and electrical safety when introducing new processes, prototype hardware, or test methods.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Degree in Electrical Engineering or related field; Bachelor's with 1+ years experience in control panel design, PLC programming, or test/automation equipment, or Master's with research or professional engineering experience.

Form Energy is hiring a Electronics Test Engineer II for the AMU (Auxiliary Management Unit) to join our BMS Test team. In this role, you will be responsible for executing design verification and validation testing at the component, board, and system level for our AMU hardware. 

 

Physically, the AMU PCBA sits inside the AMU Panel assembly along with the HIgh Voltage DC Shunt board which is responsible for measuring efficiency of our system, UPS, and PSUs. It acts as a critical zone controller responsible for communication, network security, high-voltage/high-current sensing, power distribution, actuation, safety/fault management, and UPS management.

 

You will ensure that AMU electronics meet stringent functional, reliability, safety, and compliance requirements through structured test campaigns. You’ll collaborate closely with hardware, firmware, and systems engineers to validate designs that are central to the safe and reliable operation of our multi-megawatt battery systems.This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the scaling of our battery technology and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!

 

Relocation assistance is available. 

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Test Strategy & DVP: Be part of the Development for comprehensive test plans, DVP&Rs, and verification protocols for the AMU PCBA and its integrated panel assembly components.

 - Communication Protocol Verification: Validate safety-critical and non-safety communication interfaces including CAN-FD (to ZMUs), Ethernet (to ZMUs and upstream QMU), and dedicated RS485 (for UPS management).

 - Sensing Subsystem Validation: Execute test setups to verify precision sensing capabilities: Pack HV voltage (-1 to 1600V via HVDC Shunt resistor divider), Pack HV current (-500A to 500A via shunt R4), 48V PSU/UPS monitoring (0-60V), 48V total current draw (0-40A), and auxiliary temperatures.

 - Actuation & Power Distribution: Verify HV contactor control (pack connect/disconnect), heater SSR control, and power routing from dual 48V PSUs and the 48V UPS down to the ZMUs.

 - Safety & Fault Management: Rigorously test Hardware Over-Current Protection, fault loop logic, and Functional Safety (FuSa) testing.

 - Data Analysis & Root-Cause: Analyze test data, generate detailed reports, and collaborate with design engineers to root-cause board or firmware anomalies found during testing.

 - Test Automation: Contribute to test automation frameworks (utilizing Pytest) to optimize repeatability and scale verification throughput.

 


WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.

 - 1+ years of experience in PCBA hardware testing. Must have robust board-level and system-level validation experience.

 - Some experience in firmware verification, utilizing Pytest or similar unit testing frameworks. Comfort with debugging tools, Linux environments, and Test-Driven Development (TDD)

 - Hands-on experience with test instrumentation (oscilloscopes, power supplies, data acquisition systems, environmental chambers).

 - Hands-on experience with high-voltage/high-current test instrumentation (power supplies, electronic loads)

 - Demonstrated ability to work with test plans, execute verification activities, and communicate findings effectively.

 - Domain Knowledge: Understanding of communication protocols (CAN-FD, Ethernet, RS485), power distribution topologies, and functional safety frameworks.

The Account Manager is responsible for overseeing private label program development with US dealers and international product lines. It serves as the primary relationship and technical support lead for key customers and service partners.

description:
Job Description:
Job Summary
The Customer Service Representative is responsible for representing StampTech by serving our customers. Requests and inquiries received via phone, email, fax, as well as direct contact from our sales force. Gaining a quick understanding of customer needs, responding promptly, and providing solutions for customers are the keys to developing and maintaining strong customer relationships. This position performs proactive product expediting and data entry to ensure a timely and accurate understanding of customer transactions. These duties are performed mainly for automotive customers in the assigned market segment of our business. This position is currently located in our Gallatin, TN facility and is expected to move to our new Portland, TN warehouse next quarter.
Company Overview
ITW Description:
Illinois Tool Works Inc. (NYSE: ITW) is a global Fortune 200 diversified manufacturing company that delivers specialized expertise, innovative thinking, and value-added products to meet critical customer needs in a variety of industries.   ITW, with approximately 14.1 billion dollars in global revenues, operates 7 major segments with businesses in 57 countries that employ approximately 45,000 women and men. These talented individuals, many of whom have specialized engineering or scientific expertise, contribute to our global leadership in innovation. We are proud of our broad portfolio of more than 16,000 active patents.
StampTech Fasteners TM Division Description:
The ITW StampTech Fastener TM Division serves the major OEMs and Tier suppliers in the North American automotive market.  The division supplies stamped metal fasteners and engineered fastener assemblies that leverage our deep-draw stamping technologies.  The annual revenue for the division is approximately $160M.  Locations include Gallatin, TN, Lexington, KY & Naugatuck, CT.
The Division drives profitability by leveraging its innovative solutions and application engineering.  In addition to ITW’s industry leading research and development capabilities, StampTech Fasteners TM enhances our customers’ competitive advantage by maintaining advanced engineering and manufacturing facilities in North America, exchanging product, process, and benchmarking information with sister units worldwide and continually improving processes, material, and designs to ensure every product provides value and meets customer expectations.
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
Relationship management of assigned key accounts.
Service customers seeking assistance with multiple issues such as returns, replacements, refunds, delivery status and backorder inquiries, problem resolution, and any other issues that may arise from the order fulfillment process.
Handle requests for expedites, exceptions, substitutions, allocations orders, and/or special problems.
Evaluate, monitor, and escalate any potential production outages that may impact customers to Management with recommendations.
Interact and coordinate with various departments to ensure on-time deliveries to customers.
Perform order entry by interpreting customer EDI releases and cums.
Analyze inventory to determine availability of SKUs based on customer demand.
Work with Accounting to resolve customer credit/pricing issues.
Act as liaison with customer to set up expedites and make sure expedite is coded properly.
Back-up Shipping office – sending ASNS, print shippers and create pick lists.
General filing and scanning.
Cross-training – all team members are trained on customer-specific guidelines and procedures.
Record customer complaints returns and non-conforming parts (return goods authorization procedures).
Portals and Automotive systems monitored and checked as required by customers.
All other duties as assigned by Manager.
QUALIFICATIONS
To perform this job successfully, the individual must be able to perform each essential duty.  The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required:
High School or GED is required.
3+ years manufacturing customer service experience - automotive preferred.
Must have strong communication skills and present a positive, professional image of ITW both internally and externally.
High sense of urgency for customer satisfaction.
Requires skill in defusing agitated situations.  Ability to effectively present pricing information, manufacturing lead-time changes and other related data to customers.
Must be capable of meeting deadlines based on customer demand.
Must be capable of perform all functions with minimal errors and omissions.
Highly proficient in MS Office suite of products
Future3/INFOR experience is a plus.
Understands at basic level minimum the ASN process.
Must be able to organize and prioritize workload and meet deadlines.
Some weekends/afterhours required on a rotating basis is required.
PHYSICAL DEMANDS
The physical demand described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essentials functions.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand; walk; use hands to fingers, handle, or feel, talk or hear; and smell. The employee frequently is required to reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to sit and stoop or crouch. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 45 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts and vibration. The employee is frequently exposed to fumes or airborne particles. title: HR Specialist
description:
Job Description:
Human Resources Specialist
ABOUT ITW MEDICAL:
ITW (NYSE: ITW) is a Fortune 300 global multi-industrial manufacturing leader with revenue of $16 billion in 2025. The company’s seven industry-leading segments leverage the unique ITW Business Model to drive solid growth with best-in-class margins and returns in markets where highly innovative, customer-focused solutions are required. ITW’s approximately 43,000 dedicated colleagues around the world thrive in the company’s decentralized and entrepreneurial culture.
ITW Medical, a division of ITW, is comprised of two highly respected brands- Coeur and Filtertek, supplying critical filtration and flow control solutions to global OEM’s, serving Surgical, Infusion, Bioprocessing and Diagnostic Imaging end markets.
Position Summary:
The Human Resources Specialist supports organizational effectiveness by collecting, analyzing, and interpreting human resources data to drive informed business decisions. This role partners with the HR Director and leaders to support workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, employee retention, compliance, compensation, training, and performance management initiatives. The HR Analyst develops actionable insights, maintains key HR metrics and dashboards, and makes recommendations that enhance talent acquisition, employee engagement, and overall organizational performance.
Duties and Responsibilities:
Analyze workforce trends and organizational metrics to identify talent gaps, skill gaps, succession planning opportunities, retention risks, and workforce needs. Provide data-driven recommendations that support organizational growth, workforce forecasting, and strategic business objectives.
Support talent management initiatives, including performance management, talent reviews, succession planning, career development, and competency framework administration. Assist with goal setting, performance evaluations, calibration activities, reporting, and the maintenance of career paths and development tools.
Lead the administration and continuous improvement of employee recognition programs by evaluating participation and effectiveness, maintaining existing initiatives, and recommending new programs that enhance employee engagement, retention, and organizational culture.
Conduct compensation analyses, including salary benchmarking, job classification reviews, pay equity assessments, and market comparisons. Present findings and recommendations to HR leadership.
Support recruitment and onboarding efforts, including full-cycle recruiting activities, onboarding program administration, employer branding initiatives, talent pipeline development, and analysis of recruiting and onboarding effectiveness metrics.
Develop and maintain relationships with external recruiting partners, educational institutions, and community organizations to support workforce needs and build diverse talent pipelines.
Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local employment laws and regulations, including data privacy, record retention, employee records management, compensation practices, and other regulatory requirements.
Conduct periodic audits of HR processes and records, including employee data, compensation, job classifications, and compliance requirements, and recommend corrective actions or process improvements as needed.
Evaluate, develop, and recommend improvements to HR policies, programs, and processes in partnership with HR leadership and site HR teams, supporting implementation and communication efforts.
Collect, validate, analyze, and maintain HR data from multiple sources including HRIS, payroll systems, surveys, exit interviews, performance evaluations, applicant tracking systems, and other workforce management tools.
Develop and maintain HR dashboards, reports, and key performance indicators (KPIs) related to headcount, turnover, retention, compensation, recruiting, onboarding, employee engagement, performance management, and workforce planning.
Perform other related duties as assigned.
Qualifications / Skills:
Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Industrial Psychology, Analytics, or a related field required.
3-5+ years of progressive Human Resources experience, including recruitment, onboarding, talent development, HR analytics and reporting.
SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or comparable certification preferred.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent verbal, written, and presentation communication skills.
Strong attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
Knowledge of recruitment, onboarding, workforce planning, compensation, benefits, and employee relations practices.
Thorough understanding of federal, state, and local employment laws and regulations.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Office Suite, PowerBi or equivalent and HR reporting tools.
Experience working with HRIS, payroll systems, applicant tracking systems (ATS), and workforce analytics platforms.
Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion.
Physical Requirements:

Ability to occasionally lift and carry up to 15 pounds.

title: Senior Electrical Engineer
description:
Job Description:
Brooks Instrument ( www.brooksinstrument.com ), an industry leader in flow and pressure instrumentation for critical applications, is seeking candidates for a Senior Electrical Engineer  position that will be based at the company headquarters in Hatfield, Pennsylvania (suburban Philadelphia). The company has manufacturing locations in Pennsylvania, Hungary, Malaysia and Korea, and also maintains sales and service offices throughout the world. Our high-tech products are used in laboratory and process applications in end markets such as: oil & gas, petrochemical, medical devices, waste water, life sciences, and analytical instruments.
Brooks is a division of ITW (Illinois Tool Works), a fortune 200 company. ITW is one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, consumables, and related service businesses. The company has operations in 56 countries and employs over 50,000 employees. These talented employees, many of whom have specialized engineering or scientific expertise, contribute to ITW’s global leadership in innovation. The company is proud of its broad portfolio of nearly 10,000 active patents, and is focused on fully leveraging its highly differentiated business model to deliver solid growth with consistent best-in-class margins and return on capital.
Basic Function
The Electrical Engineering position is part of the sustaining engineering team responsible for the design, support, and maintenance of electronic hardware and firmware for all released Brooks Instrument products. This role is a cross-functional position where both circuit design and embedded software development skills are required. This individual must be self-directed, highly motivated, and organized with strong analytical thinking and problem solving skills. They must also possess the ability to work on multiple projects and functions simultaneously in a team environment.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Design and maintain embedded hardware and firmware systems for flow and pressure control devices.
Create and maintain design documentation packages.
Perform analog circuit design and simulation including power supply circuitry (switching and linear), voltage and current I/O circuitry, as well as circuits with discrete semiconductors.
Design and simulation of digital circuits using microprocessors and associated peripheral devices in embedded systems.
Use CAD tools for schematic capture and simulation to achieve circuit design goals.
Support printed circuit board (PCB) layouts, working within 2D and 3D spatial constraints.
Translate firmware requirements into highly reliable and well-structured C/C++ embedded firmware.
Follow Brooks’ current and future best practices for hardware and firmware design.
Perform design work, preliminary testing, and coordination for agency approvals (CE, UL, RoHS).
Ability to diagnose problems and provide solutions within project constraints.
Possess abilities to take on multiple concurrent assignments under minimal supervision.
Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.
Strong teamwork skills.
Ability to follow all safety procedures.
Other duties as assigned.
Knowledge , Skills and Abilities
Extensive knowledge of embedded electronics, including analog & digital circuit design as well as firmware development required.

title: Supply/Demand Planner
description:
Job Description:
About Us:
ITW Car Care is a division of Illinois Tool Works (ITW), specializing in automotive aftermarket products. The division offers a diverse portfolio of brands such as Rain-X wiper blades, visibility enhancing products, and water-repellent treatments, including our 2-in-1 Glass Cleaner. Black Magic to support all your wheel and tire needs including Tire Wet.
Position Summary:
We are hiring two Supply/Demand Planners, with opportunities at either the Planner I or Planner II level based on experience.
These roles are responsible for balancing Finished Goods (FG), Semi-Finished Goods (SFG), and Raw Materials (RM) with customer demand through forecasting, supply planning, and cross-functional collaboration. The planners will partner with suppliers, manufacturing sites, and sales teams to achieve service, inventory, and MOH targets. Planner II candidates will also take ownership of end-to-end material planning and provide guidance to less experienced planners.
Key Responsibilities:
Demand Planning
Build and maintain statistical demand forecasts.
Track Point of Sale (POS) data and adjust the forecast to reflect changes in demand.
Bring forecast inputs to demand planning meetings with Sales and Marketing.
Supply Planning & Purchasing
Run long-term and short-term planning for Finished Goods (FG), Semi-Finished Goods (SFG/SM) and Raw Materials (RM).
Purchase FG, SFG and RM, and coordinate supplier deliveries so products arrive on time.
Calculate Market Rate of Demand (MRD) requirements for suppliers. Maintain and update the MRD system using Run Rates (RR), Lead Times (LT) and batch sizes.
Run Material Requirements Planning (MRP) in the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system to plan material and production needs.
Plan manufacturing production, working with the plants on schedules and capacity.
Inventory & Performance Management
Calculate and report key planning metrics:
- Months on Hand (MOH)
- Obsolete and Slow-Moving Inventory (OSMI)
- On-Time In-Full (OTIF)
- Run Rate (RR) and Safety Stock (SS)
- Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ)
- Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)
Analyze inventory data and recommend actions to improve Months on Hand (MOH).
Recommend and make planning parameter changes: Lead Times (LT), minimum inventory, lot sizes and order policies.
Build and maintain Power BI dashboards and Excel reports to track inventory and service performance.
Take part in supplier and manufacturing site meetings, and support the monthly Inventory Management meeting.
Apply 80/20 principles to focus planning effort on the products and customers that matter most.
Planner II Scope (in addition to the above)
Independently own the full MRD and MRP process for an assigned product portfolio.
Train and mentor Planner I team members.
Lead small improvement projects in planning and sourcing.
Qualifications:
Required
Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Business, or a related field.
Planner I: 0–3 years of experience in supply chain, procurement or supplier coordination.
Planner II: 3–6 years of experience, including a track record of independently managing sourcing or planning projects
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work effectively with large data sets.
Experience with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems and Material Requirements Planning (MRP) processes.
Preferred
Experience in manufacturing or production planning.
Familiarity with Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) / Integrated Business Planning (IBP) and 80/20 methodology.
APICS/ASCM certification: Certified in Planning and Inventory Management (CPIM) or Certified Supply Chain Professional (CSCP).
Technical Skills
Advanced Microsoft Excel: pivot tables, XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH, advanced formulas and data modeling.
Power BI: building dashboards and reports for inventory, forecast and service metrics.
MRP / ERP systems: running Material Requirements Planning and maintaining planning parameters.
MRD: maintaining MRD calculations and system updates.
Statistical forecasting methods and tools.
Key Competencies
Analytical thinking and attention to detail
Clear communication with suppliers, manufacturing sites and commercial teams
Takes ownership and follows through
Continuous improvement mindset
Physical Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Primarily performs work in an office environment with frequent use of a computer, telephone, and other standard office equipment.
Requires prolonged periods of sitting and working at a computer, including extensive use of a keyboard, mouse, and multiple software applications.
Frequently communicates with suppliers, manufacturing facilities, sales teams, and other stakeholders via phone, video conference, and email.
Must be able to review, analyze, and interpret large amounts of data and reports, requiring close visual acuity and sustained concentration.
Occasionally required to stand, walk, reach, bend, stoop, and move throughout office and manufacturing environments.
May occasionally lift, carry, push, or pull materials and office equipment weighing up to 15 pounds.
Ability to travel occasionally to manufacturing sites, supplier locations, or company meetings as business needs require.
Must be able to operate in both office and plant environments, including exposure to varying noise levels and production activities during site visits.
Work Environment
Work is performed primarily in a professional office setting with periodic visits to manufacturing and warehouse facilities.
During plant visits, appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) may be required in accordance with site safety policies.
Position may require flexibility to support multiple manufacturing facilities, suppliers, and time zones to ensure uninterrupted supply chain operations.

description:

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
The opportunity:
Advancing minimally invasive care requires more than great technology — it requires people who grow with the company, lead with intention, and bring their best to every challenge. The Director, Enterprise Learning will shape how we build capability from the inside out: ensuring every employee, manager, and director has the knowledge, skills, and mindset to perform and grow.
We're looking for someone who sees learning as a business discipline, not a support function. Someone who starts with strategy — understanding where Intuitive is headed and what capabilities will get us there — and works backward to design learning that actually moves the needle. A builder who combines learning design expertise with sharp business judgment, and who knows how to measure whether any of it is working.
This role covers role agnostic enterprise learning below the VP level: individual contributor development, manager learning, director learning, and employee onboarding. It's a broad remit that requires both vision and execution — and a leader who can do both.
What you'll lead:
You'll report directly to the VP, Global Talent and own the strategy, design, and delivery of enterprise-wide learning programs that are connected to business priorities, deliver measurable impact, and built to last. This isn't about building a curriculum library — it's about building capability that shows up in business results.
What this looks like:
Anchor learning to business strategy. Partner closely with HR Business Partners, business leaders, and the broader Talent team to understand where the company is going and what capabilities will be required to get there. Translate that into a multi-year enterprise learning strategy with clear priorities, measurable outcomes, and a coherent point of view on what we build, buy, or curate.
Design learning that works. Lead the design and delivery of learning experiences across the full employee population — from onboarding through director-level development. Apply modern instructional design principles across a range of modalities: in-person, digital, cohort-based, on-demand, and AI-enabled. Prioritize approaches that fit how people actually learn at work.
Own manager and director development. Build and continuously evolve learning programs for managers and directors that are practical, relevant, and grounded in what Intuitive needs from its people leaders. Work closely with HR Business Partners to ensure programs address real capability gaps, not just generic leadership topics.
Deliver a best-in-class onboarding experience. Design and steward an onboarding experience that accelerates time-to-productivity, connects new employees to Intuitive's mission and culture, and sets a strong foundation for long-term engagement and performance.
Make learning measurable. Define clear success metrics for every major program and build the infrastructure to track them. Move beyond attendance and satisfaction scores — connect learning outcomes to performance, retention, and business impact. Use data to make honest calls about what's working and what isn't.
Bring modern learning approaches to life. Stay close to how the learning landscape is evolving — AI-enabled personalization, digital learning platforms, cohort learning, nudge-based reinforcement — and bring the right innovations into Intuitive in ways that are practical and scalable, not just novel.
Build and lead a high-performing team. Lead a team of learning professionals with clarity, high standards, and genuine investment in their development. Create an environment where craft matters, outcomes are tracked, and continuous improvement is the norm.
Partner across HR and the business. Work closely with Talent Management, HR Business Partners, People Analytics, and I&D to ensure enterprise learning is integrated into the broader talent strategy — and that programs reflect and reinforce an inclusive, high-performance culture.
Qualifications
What you'll bring:
Learning strategy and design expertise: Significant experience designing and delivering enterprise learning programs across multiple audiences and modalities — from onboarding through senior individual contributors and people leaders. You understand instructional design deeply and apply it with both rigor and pragmatism.
Business acumen: You think like a business leader. You understand how Intuitive creates value, what's driving the strategy, and how to connect learning investments to business outcomes. You can hold your own in conversations with senior leaders about priorities, trade-offs, and ROI.
Modern learning fluency: Genuine familiarity with the evolving learning landscape — AI-enabled learning tools, digital platforms, cohort-based models, on-demand content strategies, and data-driven personalization. You know what's worth adopting and how to bring it in thoughtfully.
Measurement and outcomes orientation: A track record of defining meaningful success metrics for learning programs and using data to drive decisions. You're not satisfied with completion rates — you want to know whether learning changed behavior and moved business results.
Stakeholder influence: Strong ability to build relationships with and influence senior business leaders and HR partners. You can translate learning strategy into language that resonates with business audiences, and you earn credibility through follow-through and results.
People leadership: You lead with clarity and high standards, invest genuinely in your team's growth, and create an environment where excellent work is the expectation.
Operational excellence: You can manage a complex portfolio of programs, vendors, and priorities without losing sight of quality. You build systems and processes that scale — and you know when to simplify.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in Learning & Development, Organizational Psychology, Instructional Design, or a related field preferred.
12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise learning, with demonstrated success leading learning strategy and design across a large, complex organization.
Experience with AI-enabled learning tools and modern digital learning platforms strongly preferred.
Ability to travel approximately 20% of the time.
**Please note this position requires being onsite in our Sunnyvale, CA office 3 days per week.

description:

We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function
The Lead Director of Photography is a creative and craft leader within Intuitive’s Studio, responsible for advancing the visual language of moving image, motion, and photography across Brand & Creative.
This is a hands-on role for someone with strong visual instincts, a clear point of view, and the range to move between creative development and execution. They can define how something should look and feel, then step behind the camera and make it happen.
The Lead DP partners closely with designers, art directors, writers, producers, editors, motion designers, and, as needed, strategy and social teams. They contribute as a creative peer to senior creative talent and executive creative leadership, confidently advocating for ideas while remaining curious, adaptable, and open to feedback from anyone.
Moving image is central to the role. The Lead DP also leads the development of Studio’s photography practice, creating high-end photography on select projects and elevating standards, practices, and output across the team. This responsibility does not include direct management of photographers.
We’re looking for someone who loves making things, brings fresh thinking, shares knowledge generously, and is as willing to do the heavy lifting as they are to lead the room.
What You’ll Do
Define and evolve our visual language
Advance Studio’s approach to moving image, motion, and photography in close partnership with Creative.
Contribute from the earliest stages of development, translating ideas, stories, and brand objectives into distinct visual approaches.
Bring production craft into the development of ideas, helping shape what we make and how we make it.
Explore new approaches to shooting, editing, lighting, composition, and motion that strengthen storytelling and help evolve the brand’s look and feel.
Lead cinematography and filmmaking
Serve as lead DP across Studio productions, owning the approach to camera, lighting, lenses, composition, movement, coverage, and image capture.
Develop treatments, visual references, shot lists, and storyboards, including rough sketches when useful.
Direct projects, talent, interviews, or scenes when the assignment calls for it.
Lead camera and lighting crews with clear direction, thoughtful preparation, and sound creative and technical judgment.
Adapt to changing conditions while protecting the story, creative intent, and quality of the work.
Elevate the photography practice
Shoot high-end photography on select assignments that benefit from your expertise.
Establish and continually raise standards for lighting, composition, technique, and execution across photography produced by Studio and its partners.
Improve photography workflows, equipment practices, and quality standards.
Guide and mentor teammates and external partners through constructive feedback and shared expertise.
Shape the story through post
Partner with editors and motion designers to develop new approaches to structure, pacing, rhythm, movement, and sound.
Bring ideas and constructive creative challenge that help teammates expand how they tell stories.
Contribute hands-on editing support when needed.
On larger projects, contribute to casting, music, editorial, color, and finishing, staying engaged through final delivery.
Work independently and collaboratively
Independently plan and execute smaller shoots, including assignments without a dedicated producer.
Collaborate effectively within larger teams of creatives, producers, directors, agencies, production partners, and specialized crews.
Recommend an approach and production scale appropriate to the idea, budget, schedule, and intended result.
Prepare thoroughly, solve problems resourcefully, and follow through on commitments.
Strengthen the team
Lead through the quality of your work, the clarity of your ideas, and how you treat people.
Share knowledge and mentor teammates through the work, helping develop their craft, judgment, and confidence.
Give useful feedback, welcome different perspectives, and share credit.
Contribute beyond your own assignments to improve the work and capabilities of Studio and Brand & Creative.
What You Bring
A strong body of work demonstrating accomplished cinematography, high-quality photography, and thoughtful visual storytelling. Please identify your contribution to each project.
Deep practical knowledge of cameras, lenses, lighting, composition, movement, exposure, and image capture.
The ability to connect visual decisions to a story, audience, and creative idea.
The confidence and judgment to present ideas, lead a shoot, and collaborate as a peer with senior creative partners.
The ability to communicate visually through references, treatments, shot lists, storyboards, or sketches.
Working editing proficiency and an understanding of editorial, motion, music, color, and finishing.
Resourcefulness across small independent assignments and larger productions.
Curiosity, initiative, reliability, and a commitment to developing both your own work and the people around you.
How You Work Matters
Low ego is essential. You bring conviction without defensiveness, take feedback seriously regardless of its source, and treat everyone with respect. You remain willing to execute the details and do the heavy lifting, regardless of experience or seniority.
We welcome both emerging creative leaders ready for broader responsibility and experienced practitioners eager to contribute and mentor. Your work, judgment, and approach to collaboration matter.
Travel: Approximately 20% travel is expected, depending on production needs.
Required Skills, Experience, and Training
12+ years of experience
Experience working in or closely with Brand & Creative teams.
A bachelor's degree in film, design, media arts, communications, or adjacent fields; equivalent professional experience is also acceptable.
