performance, safety and user-facing features of the da Vinci™ Surgical System, Intuitive’s flagship product.
We’re looking for a high energy, experienced embedded software engineer to take technical ownership
across our embedded platform software stack.
In this role, you will lead board bring-up initiatives, drive architectural decision for our next-generation platforms, and serve as a technical anchor for the team – mentoring junior engineers and collaborating cross-functionally with hardware, system software, and FPGA teams. You will own critical subsystems supporting video networking, UI display, and machine learning capabilities of Da Vinci 5 while driving improvements in robustness, reliability, manufacturability, and serviceability.
Essential Job Duties
Lead board bring-up activities for next generation-based platforms including bootloader configuration, BSP customization, peripheral driver integration and system validation – taking end-to-end ownership from initial power-on through production readiness.
Own development and drive the technical direction of embedded software for video networking, UI display, and machine learning applications on Linux-based systems – including architectural decisions, code review and performance optimization.
Design and own comprehensive test strategies to validate board functionality, peripheral interfaces, and system performance metrics – including defining acceptance criteria and driving resolution of complex hardware-software integration issues.
Partner with and technically guide hardware engineers to identify, root-cause and resolve board-level issues during early development phases – serving as the primary software interface for cross-functional hardware bring-up
Architect and lead the development of automated test frameworks for board validation and regression testing – establishing scalable infrastructure usable across multiple platform variants.
Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through code reviews, technical guidance, and hands-on debugging support – actively contributing to the growth of the team.
Author and maintain technical documentation including design specifications, bring-up procedures, and failure analysis reports in compliance with FDA-regulated development processes.
Required Education, Skills & Experience
Minimum of 8 years of related experience and a Bachelor's degree; or 6 years experience and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 3 years of experience; or equivalent experience
Expert-level proficiency in C or C++ for embedded systems development, including memory management, real-time constraints, and performance-critical code
Experience in bare-metal, embedded Linux, including kernel internals, custom device driver development, BSP bring-up, and user space application development
Proficiency with embedded development and debugging tools including GDB, JTAG, logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, and cross-compilation toolchains
Proven hands-on experience with hardware interfaces and protocols (I2C, I2S, T1S, SPI, UART, USB, Ethernet, CAN) – including bring-up debugging, and driver development for each
Debugging and root-cause analysis skills, with a track record of resolving complex, multi-layer Hardware-FPGA-software integration failures in time-critical environments
Demonstrated ability to mentor and technically develop junior and mid-level engineers
Effective written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation and cross-functional team collaboration
Preferred Skills & Experience
Hands-on experience with NVIDIA Jetson platforms (TX2/Xavier/Orin or similar) or comparable ARM-based SOCs in a production embedded environment
Hands-on experience with GPU acceleration (CUDA) and hardware-accelerated inference frameworks (TensorRT) in production embedded systems
Experience with QNX RTOS or other real-time operating systems in safety-critical applications.
Proficiency in Python and bash scripting for test automation, bootup design, and build system integration

description:

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Human Factors Design Engineer (HFDE) is part of the Human Factors (HF) organization that aims to maximize usability and desirability of Intuitive products while minimizing risk through scientific research and usability engineering. Broadly, HFDE is focused on research and design within product development of new robotic systems, instruments and accessories. This role is more exclusively focused on Human Robotic Interaction Research, Neurorobotics, and Neural Interfaces.
HFDE helps de-risk design strategies within product development through a range of formative research activities and hands-on design engineering activities that inform the definition of user requirements and user interface design requirements underlying the user experience of Intuitive products.
HFDE conducts research that is focused on the psychology, biomechanics, and physiology of end users’ underlying performance associated with robotic teleoperations. This position will generate evidence to provide strategic insight into “what”, “why”, and “how much” end users differ in learning and performance across a range of products. This role functions in ambiguous and strategic stages of product development that involve the ability to position and conduct experimental research within a business.
This role demands extensive follow-through to translate, communicate, ideate, prototype, and build novel evidence-based strategies, tools, and concepts that operationalize and inform the “intuitiveness” of commercialized and future products. This role demands quick changes in direction with capacity to define and implement strategies that have visibility across business units while maintaining focus on tactical details. This role is a unique engineering and scientific opportunity with the expectation that knowledge and skills can be applied to experimental behavioral and neuroscientific research that actionably informs product design strategies for future development, inform product development, and establish product claims with state-of-the-art human-robot interfaces.
The HFDE position reports to a Manager within the broader HF organization at Intuitive.
Essential Job Duties
Apply deep expertise in robotics, HRI, and mixed-methods research to identify unmet user needs, performance limitations, and opportunities for future product innovation.
Independently generate, prioritize, and communicate actionable design insights that shape product strategy, influence development priorities, and advance human factors capabilities.
De-risk design strategies focused on the analysis of human performance, workflow, and usability factors, while identifying and mitigating systemic usability risks across product lines.
Serve as the human factors lead for complex initiatives, partnering with engineering, product management, quality, and regulatory teams to drive usability-centered design decisions.
Influence product and business decisions by balancing user needs, safety, usability, technical feasibility, and organizational priorities.
Lead the definition and management of usability design inputs across robotic systems, instruments, and accessories, translating research findings into actionable user and interface requirements.
Conduct literature reviews that justify research strategy and study design
Conduct experiments end-to-end ranging in scale and complexity, including data processing and analysis from multimodal data capture
Translate scientific evidence to a range of internal and external stakeholders into actional recommendations for product design strategies, product requirements, or product claims
Develop and evaluate conceptual prototypes that communicate design strategies, performance considerations, and future product concepts.
Data extraction, transformation, processes, analysis and visualization with multiple data sources from biometrics, psychometrics, and system data logs from lab-based experiments and field-based experiments
Prototype and iterate on designs, develop tests, and deliver high-quality software in Python or C++ required for ML performance modeling
Manage updates on systems configurations for reliable data capture pipeline from lab-based and field-based experiments
Build and validate experimental conditions within virtual and physical environments
Develop and validate novel and OTS bioinstrumentation and psychometrics that can be implemented in experiments to reliably measure individual differences related to human performance
Author and maintain early stage human factors engineering deliverables, ensuring compliance with design controls, usability engineering processes, and regulatory requirements. Mentor peers and project teams in applying HF methodologies, frameworks, and best practices while fostering innovation through the integration of user insights and cross-functional expertise.
Required Skills and Experience
​​​​ Minimum 8 - 15 years relevant experience in industry.
Minimum 6 years relevant human subjects.
Ability to campaign and drive user-centered design strategies, as well as usability engineering principles to product research, development, and design.
Ability to independently propose and position research plans across a range of products and a myriad of internal and/or external stakeholders
Ability to develop experimental conditions and stimuli in virtual and physical environments.
Ability to translate findings from studies into product requirements for complex, software-controlled electro-mechanical medical device.
Experience with authoring and reviewing scientific manuscripts.
Expertise in robotic systems, including mechanical design (kinematics/ mechanisms), sensing and perception, control systems, software engineering (programming/ simulation) and human-robotic interaction.
Ability to work with and across various groups and levels of management within a matrixed organization.
Required Education and Training
Minimum post-graduate degree in Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Biomedical Engineer, Bioengineering, Psychology, Neuroscience, Biomechanics with emphasis on Human-Robotic Interactions.
Working Conditions
Ability to travel internationally as well as domestically (up to 25%).
Primarily office-based set schedule working model.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience in research on Neuromotor/ Sensorimotor Control and Learning
Experience in research on Neuroscience, a plus
Experience in Computational Psychology or Data Science, a plus.
Experience in Differential Psychology, a plus.
Experience with bioinstrumentation, a plus.
Experience in medical device, or similar regulated industry, a plus.

The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the daVinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.

Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.

Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.

Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.

Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.

Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.

Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.

Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.

Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.

Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.

Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.

Team oriented with a commercial mindset.

Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

Job Description
The Associate, Renewables Asset Management is responsible for maximizing the value and profitability of Invenergy Services' contracts through effective customer relationship management and commercial oversight. Serving as a primary customer interface, this role builds trusted partnerships, ensures contract compliance, and drives successful business outcomes across assigned contracts. As a senior individual contributor, the Associate independently manages customer relationships and commercial matters while collaborating across the organization to support strong operational and financial performance.
Responsibilities
Customer & Contract Management
Independently manage a portfolio of renewable energy service contracts and serve as the primary relationship manager for assigned customers.
Build trusted customer relationships and lead customer-facing meetings and business reviews.
Ensure fulfillment of contractual obligations and proactively identify and address commercial risks, disputes, and areas of non-compliance.
Lead commercial discussions and negotiate resolutions to contractual issues, change requests, claims, and disputes.
Partner with customers and internal stakeholders to improve asset performance, operational outcomes, and financial results.
Identify opportunities for contract renewals, service expansions, aftermarket offerings, and other value-added services.
Financial Performance
Manage the financial performance of assigned contracts and portfolios, identifying opportunities to enhance value and profitability.
Support budget development, forecasting, variance analysis, and other financial reviews as required under customer agreements.
Evaluate and develop business cases for operational improvements, cost-saving initiatives, and aftermarket opportunities.
Develop reports, presentations, and analyses to communicate financial and operational performance and key insights to customers and internal stakeholders.
Support achievement of contract margin targets, profitability objectives, forecast accuracy, and financial performance for assigned customer portfolios.
Operations
Collaborate with Operations, Performance Engineering, Electrical Engineering, SCADA Engineering, and other cross-functional teams to optimize asset performance.
Monitor key operational metrics and coordinate resolution of performance, availability, and reliability issues.
Coordinate major maintenance activities, equipment replacement strategies, and other initiatives impacting asset performance.
Coordinate internal resources across Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Legal, Finance, and HSE to resolve customer issues and deliver contractual commitments.
Support the onboarding of new contracts and assets, ensuring a seamless transition into commercial operations.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related quantitative discipline.
Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in asset management, power generation, renewable energy, or a related industry.
Experience managing customer relationships and working directly with customers.
Experience administering and managing commercial contracts.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Effective communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills.
Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial analysis.
Experience with standard financial metrics and analyses, including NPV, IRR, and DCF models.
Occasional travel required.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in the renewable energy industry.
Experience managing complex customer relationships and commercial matters.
Experience working across Operations, Engineering, Finance, Legal, and other cross-functional organizations.
Experience identifying commercial opportunities, resolving contractual issues, or supporting contract negotiations.

The Procurement Manager for Innovation connects Kraft Heinz business strategy, brand ambition, and supplier capability to bring new products to life. Job Description
Job Purpose
​​The Principal Scientist for CX Product Insights is the technical authority and methodologist for consumer experience research for Away From Home initiatives. You architect fit-for-purpose CX learning strategies across the end-to-end product lifecycle, from front-end exploration and ideation through launch readiness, ensuring methodological rigor, evidence quality, and decision-ready synthesis that accelerates innovation. You translate consumer needs into clear product and packaging experience requirements, influence cross-functional teams toward consumer- and customer-centric decisions, and balance speed vs. rigor based on decision risk. You elevate functional capability through coaching, playbooks/toolkits, and ways of working, and guide internal teams and suppliers to the right level of rigor for the decision at hand. You’ll partner closely with R&D (Product & Process Development, Packaging, Sensory), Marketing/Brand, Insights, Analytics, Culinary, and external suppliers to ensure consumer learning is converted into practical product, packaging, and technical decisions.
​
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​Provide CX technical leadership for the Away From Home team, defining key learning needs tied to business and technical decisions at each development milestone.
​Serve as subject matter expert (SME) for product and packaging design consumer research, bringing deep methodological expertise across qualitative and quantitative approaches.
​Architect end-to-end CX learning plans from upstream exploration to downstream validation, with clear decision framing, success criteria, and evidence standards aligned to risk and timelines.
​Translate complex consumer experience insights into actionable experience requirements that inform product and packaging design, managing tradeoffs and defining what success looks like.
​Lead high-stakes stakeholder readouts with compelling decision narratives, synthesizing insights and tailoring technical depth to both executive and technical audience.
​Serve as technical consultant on away from home product and pack methods and research design, best fit to the learning objectives that align with specific operators and venue types.
​Evaluate, pilot, and standardize emerging CX methods and analytics (including vendor capabilities), documenting best practices, limitations, and evidence thresholds before scaling.
​Coach and upskill scientists and partners through playbooks, training, and consultative support that embed CX rigor, curiosity, and storytelling excellence across functions.
​Oversee vendor strategy and performance: capability alignment, quality assurance, data integrity, and delivery expectations.
​Manage multiple simultaneous workstreams with disciplined prioritization, documentation, and strong stakeholder communication in a fast paced innovation environment.
​Provide continuity and backup coverage for the CX leadership team as needed.
​Ensure compliance with data integrity, privacy, and internal research governance requirements.​
Expected Experience & Required Skills
​​Bachelor’s degree minimum (Consumer Behavior, Psychology, Marketing Research, Engineering, Food Science, Human Factors, Industrial Design, or related STEM field), advanced degree preferred
​Minimum of 8+ years (BS), 7+ years (MS) or 6+ years (PhD) in consumer/product research, consumer experience, or applied insights supporting innovation, product development and commercialization.
​CPG or food & beverage experience strongly preferred, with demonstrated progression in technical expertise, including independent research strategy development, methodological leadership, and influencing cross-functional product and packaging innovation decisions.
​Experience in product consumer research to support away from home product R&D initiatives
​Recognized expertise across CX research methods (qualitative and quantitative), including end-to-end study design, instrument development, analysis planning, synthesis, and storytelling; ability to select methods based on decision risk and learning objectives.
​Proven ability to influence product and packaging innovation/renovation decisions by translating consumer needs into clear experience requirements and decision criteria
​Direct experience in consumer research methodology focused on packaging technical design
​Strong technical oversight: expert scoping, critical review of study quality, and ability to QA vendor work (methods, analysis, and interpretation).
​Clear, succinct communication across audiences, including leadership-level implications, tradeoffs, and uncertainty/limitations.
​Demonstrated capability building: coaching, technical training, and establishing best practices/standards in a matrixed organization.
​Strong cross-functional leadership and stakeholder management; sound escalation judgment and ability to correct misinterpretations of evidence.
​Strong prioritization and independent execution across a complex portfolio with multiple concurrent projects.
​Working proficiency with quantitative/statistical interpretation used in CX and product testing; comfort using and overseeing common research platforms and analysis tools (survey/testing platforms, analysis packages, dashboards/BI), consistent with internal standards.
​Ability to travel up to 20% of the time.​
Work Environment & Schedule
We believe the office is a critical driver of innovation, connection, and development, but also realize providing flexibility to our employees is critical. To create a more agile and modern workplace, this position will be able to work virtually for up to two days each week and will be expected to work in-person at the assigned work location at least three days per work week.

Overview
Microsoft Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft’s expanding Cloud Infrastructure and responsible for powering Microsoft’s “Intelligent Cloud” mission. SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft’s over 200 online businesses including Bing, MSN, Office 365, Xbox Live, Teams, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform globally with our server and data center infrastructure, security and compliance, operations, globalization, and manageability solutions. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide and we are looking for passionate engineers to help achieve that mission.
As Microsoft’s cloud business continues to grow, the ability to deploy new offerings and HW infrastructure on time, in high volume, with high quality and lowest cost is of paramount importance. To achieve this goal, the SCHIE team is instrumental in defining and delivering measures of success for hardware design, qualification, fleet support, scale, and sustainability related to Microsoft cloud hardware.
Azure Memory and Storage Center of Excellence (AMS CoE) is part of the SCHIE organization focusing on memory and storage devices going into the cloud hardware servers. AMS provides memory and storage solutions to Azure and drives memory and storage suppliers to deliver high quality products that meet our requirements. AMS CoE also leads Azure Fault Prediction and Detection (AFPD) , the platform that predicts, detects and repairs hardware failures across the Azure fleet.
We are looking for a Cloud Principal Hardware Engineer to scale AFPD across hardware components in the Azure fleet and to lead hands-on hardware resiliency for the platform.
The opportunity:
Every hour a server sits unhealthy is an hour of lost customer capacity. AFPD turns hardware, firmware and OS telemetry into early detection and prediction of failures, moves customer workloads off failing nodes, and sends a targeted repair for the part that failed. Repair outcomes and supplier failure analysis then improve the next rule or model.
You’ll work across the full server platform, including storage, memory, power supplies, CPUs, GPUs, NICs, HBAs/FPGAs, cabling, and other critical hardware components. As a trusted SME (Subject Matter Expert) you’ll help identify potential failures, improve hardware reliability, and prevent disruptions before they impact customers. Your impact will be felt at massive scale . Across millions of nodes, every reliability improvement translates into fewer customer VM interruptions, faster restoration of online capacity, and a more resilient cloud infrastructure. Why this role:
Your impact shows up in fleet availability and customer uptime, quarter over quarter. You will set the hardware direction for a platform that influences production infrastructure at a scale, and you will work directly with Azure engineering, component teams and leading hardware suppliers.

Lead failure analysis across server components: characterize failure modes from fleet telemetry and logs and confirm root cause with repair results and supplier failure analysis.

Leverage AI-powered tools and data-driven insights to analyze hardware failures, identify emerging reliability trends, and proactively improve server performance and availability.

As a Logistics Technician, you will perform cycle audits, execute incoming/outgoing deliveries, coordinate security escorts for third-party vendors, and document inbound and outbound deliveries. Customer Service

Becomes familiar with guidelines set by the Microsoft contractual agreements with suppliers and maintains a strong customer focus. Recognizes potential stakeholder impact of external and internal events and issues, communicates potential impact, and plans for impact accordingly.

Ensures DBD serial number matches with database. Supports decommissioning servers, maintaining compliance and meeting Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
Fleet Management Performs weekly vehicle inspections.
Inbound and Outbound Logistics
Performs data entry to document inbound and outbound packages. Executes incoming/outgoing deliveries as instructed by management (e.g. purchase order [PO] receiving, Rack Movement Supervisor [RMS] activities). Ensures accurate documentation of incoming and outgoing deliveries as well as records. Applies appropriate customs documentations and standards for outbound packages.
IT Inventory Management Develops working knowledge of stock control and inventory management practices and procedures. Performs cycle audits and data corrections to ensure all inventory controls are met and helps report and reconcile inventory discrepancies. Ensures detailed physical inventory tracking and staging, identifying opportunities to improve inventory and address space constraints. Performs material movement, including shipping/receiving and inventory management per standard process.
Operational Excellence Follows existing procedures to run processes and ensures execution with consistency, accuracy, and timeliness of delivery. Engages in Task Hazard Analysis (THA) consistently for every task to be performed and ensures sign off from appropriate person for any related risks. Conducts rack movement activities, supporting training on devices and tools and upholding safety standards. Follows established protocols on dealing with unsafe materials out of containment, leveraging safety alert system, escalating to management, and properly disposing of them.
Tactical Shift Management Performs assigned tasks and escalates issues during high-volume work activity or escalation-based situations. Seeks guidance from management before proceeding with the next step of a process. Begins monitoring inbound and outbound schedules, escalating deviations from scheduling, with guidance.

Working 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.

Processes failed vendor hardware devices using online/other tools, including information processing, packaging, shipment, and receipt of return for Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) and non-RMA devices. Performs manual return processes for non-RMA failed parts. Begins to perform manual ordering processes of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts. Follows all Service Level Agreements (SLAs) related to RMA and non-RMA warranty process.

AI & Human Systems brings together researchers and applied scientists who have been part of the Fairness, Accountability, Transparency, and Ethics in AI  (FATE),  Sociotechnical Alignment Center  (STAC),  Economics and Computation , and  Computational Social Science  (CSS) groups. As a Senior AI Engineer on the Microsoft Office AI team, you will bring these experiences to hundreds of millions of people.
Achieving this vision starts with understanding the work itself, directly from the people doing it. Every professional domain has its own workflows, terminology, constraints, business rules, and standards for what constitutes a good outcome, much of which remains buried in long-tail domain knowledge. You will work closely with customers, users, and domain experts to discover how work happens in practice, identify high-value opportunities for AI, and rapidly validate ideas against real customer needs. From there, you will translate ambiguous problems into practical product and technical decisions: which domain-specific workflows agents should handle, what knowledge and tools they need, how much autonomy they should have, and where human judgment remains essential. As a Senior AI Engineer , you will turn those insights into systems that work in real customer environments. You will prototype, build, evaluate, deploy, debug, and continuously improve production-grade domain agents across Copilot in Office and Copilot Cowork, working hands-on across grounding, orchestration, tool use, enterprise permissions, reliability, observability, and evaluation. You will collaborate directly with customers to validate solutions against real enterprise data, existing applications, security boundaries, and operational constraints, using production feedback to diagnose failures and iterate quickly.

Working 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.

   - Define equipment interfaces, control modes, permissives, interlocks and failure responses between OEM packages and the plant control system.

   - Work with internal engineering teams and equipment vendors to build and validate representative models of the electrical system, from the generation plant and utility interconnection through the data center distribution system to representative GPU rack loads.

description:
About the team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence (AGI) benefits all of humanity. Our Go-To-Market (GTM) organization helps customers adopt and scale OpenAI’s products and platform.

The GTM Strategy & Planning team sits within Revenue Operations and works at the intersection of GTM Leadership, Strategic Finance, and the broader business. We shape how OpenAI invests, organizes, and scales its revenue organization, translating company ambitions into actionable growth strategies, financial targets, capacity plans, and investment decisions.

Our work spans OpenAI’s global GTM organization, including Sales, Technical Success, Partnerships, and emerging businesses. We partner closely with senior leadership to ensure our resources support the highest-impact opportunities as the business grows.

About the role

We’re looking for a highly analytical and strategic operator to help shape OpenAI’s GTM growth strategy and operating plan.

In this role, you’ll tackle some of the most important questions facing our revenue organization: Where should we invest to accelerate growth? How should we allocate resources across markets, segments, and customer motions? What level of productivity can we expect as we scale? How do we translate ambitious financial goals into executable plans?

You’ll own planning and analytical workstreams spanning revenue targets, investment strategy, capacity and productivity modeling, and GTM organizational design. Working closely with Strategic Finance, GTM Leadership, and cross-functional partners, you’ll develop rigorous, data-backed recommendations that inform executive decisions.

This role is ideal for someone who combines strong financial and analytical skills with strategic judgment, thrives in ambiguity, and can move between detailed modeling and executive-level decision-making.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or New York, NY.

In this role, you will:

 - Partner with GTM Leadership and Strategic Finance to translate company financial objectives into growth strategies, resource allocation decisions, and operating plans across regions, segments, and functions.

Quality & Yield Optimization: Collaborate with Quality and Reliability teams to analyze failure data, continuously refine test coverage, enforce strict BOM validation, and drive high First Pass Yield (FPY) across manufacturing lines.
Manufacturing Data & Scale: Build scalable test infrastructure and data pipelines that convert growing volumes of manufacturing and field data into actionable insights for faster failure detection, predictive quality, yield optimization, and continuous improvement.

Passion for Excellence: Apply a relentless focus on quality, precision, and continuous improvement to ensure every system meets the highest standards and delivers a dependable customer experience.
Solid State Drive (SSD) / Flash Expertise: Hands-on background with flash memory architectures, NVMe/PCIe drive protocols, SSD firmware integration, and drive-level (L6) failure analysis within enterprise or hyperscale environments.
Manufacturing & NPI Testing Experience: Proven track record running manufacturing test development, BOM validation, and hardware bring-up through NPI/DVT phases in high-volume compute or storage manufacturing setups.
Technical & Diagnostic Proficiency: Deep expertise in Linux operating systems, PXE boot frameworks, BMC/IPMI interfaces, low-level storage diagnostics, and scripting languages (Python, Bash).
Cross-Functional & Vendor Leadership: Strong ability to interface with external ODMs, contract manufacturers, and cross-functional internal teams to debug line issues and enforce quality standards.
Root-Cause Analysis: Sharp debugging and problem-solving skills spanning hardware, drive interface, firmware, and complex system-level interactions.
Scalability & Future Readiness: Define a scalable manufacturing test architecture that expands test coverage, automation, data collection, and analytics as customer demand, product complexity, and production volume grow—without compromising throughput, reliability, or maintainability.

location: Carneys Point, New Jersey, United States
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

Warehouse Lead - Live Sales Host, Recommerce
Quince is a retail and technology company co-founded by a team that has extensive experience transforming retail. Competitive Pay that Grows With You: Start at a $24.50 rate with an increase to $25.00 rate after a 90-day successful completion period and increases up to $27.00 over time.
Comprehensive Benefits: We offer a comprehensive suite of benefits and wellness resources to support your health, including medical, dental, and vision benefits.
Plan for the Future: Our 401(k) savings program helps you build financial security with confidence.
Love What You Wear: Enjoy generous credits toward Quince products, quality you'll be proud to own.
Professional Development: Training and an onboarding experience to set you up for success.
Responsibilities:
Host 5 live selling shows per week (via Whatnot, Ebay, Poshmark) (4 hours each) across desktop/mobile platforms
Present inventory, demonstrate product features, and articulate value propositions to drive customer engagement
Manage real-time chat interaction, answer product questions, and build community with followers
Track and achieve weekly sales targets and recovery rate minimums
Conduct pre-show inventory audits and upload shows & inventory to platform
Stage sold inventory and organize products for pick/pack warehouse personnel post-show
Maintain professional on-camera presence and communication standards; follow brand guidelines
Provide feedback on product mix, customer feedback trends, and operational improvements
Support fellow team members during shows and cover shifts as needed
Clean up and organize studio and warehouse staging area after each show
Qualifications:
High school diploma or equivalent (GED)
2-4+ year of live selling, social media content creation, or customer-facing sales experience
Comfortable on camera; ability to present products with enthusiasm and authenticity
Strong communication skills, both written and verbal
Ability to multi-task: manage chat, demonstrate products, track sales in real-time
Reliable transportation to arrive on schedule for live show times
Flexible schedule to accommodate varying show times (some shows may be evening or weekend slots)
Comfortable with Excel, Google Sheets, Slack, and basic software
Proven attention to detail and ability to work with minimal supervision
KPIs/Success Metrics:
Streaming: Consistently deliver 20 hours per week with 98%+ attendance rate
Pre-show inventory audits: +99% independent, zero errors or discrepancies
Pre-show inventory uploads: 100% independent, zero system errors or missed shows
Live Show Performance: Sustain 90+ UPH sold across all show types
Recovery of Goods: Sustain 120%+ PCOGS consistently

Lift and carry up to 40 lbs on a regular, daily basis; occasional lifting of up to 50 lbs
Stand for extended periods throughout the workday
Use hands for grasping, organizing, and staging inventory items
Reach, bend, and stretch frequently throughout staging and inventory tasks
Ability to work in a climate-controlled warehouse environment
Clear vision and hearing to interact with customers on camera and in-person

As a M aterial Handler , you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team. The Material Handler is responsible for transporting materials from supply stores to drop-off locations using pushcart. This position completes forklift training requirements needed in order to advance to the intermediate level.

Use a pushcart to deliver materials to dedicated drop-off locations within the manufacturing facility.
Utilize trigger cards and internal applications to identify where new materials are needed, ensuring accuracy in quantities and proper procedures are followed.
Complete S&C required testing and certification hours need to pass the program.

Utilize Oracle ERP to determine part quantities, locations, and receiving history.
Meet department targets and consistently adhere to quality and safety standards.
Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
Work with departmental mentors to gain and apply feedback in pursuit of improved work quality.
Other responsibilities as assigned.

1+ years of demonstrated experience in a material handling or related role within a manufacturing environment.
Packaging, Labeling, & Shipping
Must be able to lift up 35 pounds
Good attention to detail, with the ability to determine accurate order quantities consistently.

Good communication skills (written and verbal) with the ability to articulate information efficiently and effectively to team members in a variety of production support departments.
Basic computer skills with the ability to review and respond to requests via internal applications.
Basic math skills with the ability to calculate quantities and weights.
Good interpersonal and organizational skills with the ability to understand and complete requests given by team member inside and outside of the department.
Ability to use hand tools, power tools, and precision measuring instruments such as scales and calipers.

High school Diploma/GED

location: Remote - CA; Remote - Chicago; Remote - Seattle; Remote - TX
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Samsara's Customer Success team is on the front lines of business value delivery by helping customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. Today, billing errors, concession requests, and cancellation or return exceptions land with CSMs, CS managers, and several partner teams, each holding part of the picture. No one owns the whole timeline. We are creating a dedicated Contract and Billing Resolution team to close that gap for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts.
As the Manager, Contract and Billing, you will lead this new team of 3 to 4 Contract and Billing Resolution Specialists. You will inherit work that CSMs and their managers have handled as best they can, and turn it into a function that is repeatable, measurable, and scalable: the playbook, the intake and routing, the system of record, the root-cause reporting, and the hiring and coaching of the people who do the work.
This role sits between the sales process and the finance process. A bill can look wrong because of something that happened upstream in a quote, an order form, a contract, or a segment change in Salesforce, or downstream in billing and invoicing. You and your team will figure out where it broke, regardless of which team caused it, and work across both sides to fix it. You will partner closely with Customer Success Managers, Sales, Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal, and report the repeat failures to the teams that own the underlying systems and processes.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every billing case your team resolves keeps the organizations that move goods, transport students, and restore power focused on their operations rather than on a billing dispute.
You want to build something from the ground up: This team and function are new. You will hire the team, write the playbook, and set up the systems and metrics that define how Samsara resolves billing and contract cases.
You thrive when solving problems: You figure things out, even without a clean playbook or precedent. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you find the fix that works for the customer and for Samsara, and you teach your team to do the same.
You are an investigator: You enjoy rebuilding a timeline from incomplete or conflicting records across sales and finance systems, and you stay curious until the numbers tie out.
You are a people leader: You enjoy hiring, coaching, and developing a team, and you set a high bar for quality, ownership, and follow-through.
You are a natural relationship builder: Whether with our customers or cross-functional teams at Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team, and you can maintain clear boundaries while staying warm.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals.
In this role, you will:
Build and lead a new team of 3 to 4 Contract and Billing Resolution Specialists: hire, onboard, coach, and develop them, and set clear expectations for case quality, ownership, and customer communication.
Stand up the function from scratch: take the billing, concession, and cancellation work that CSMs handle today, define what the team owns and what it does not, and turn it into a documented playbook that is repeatable and scalable.
Design and launch the system of record for billing and contract cases, working with CS Ops and Systems partners to set up intake, routing, case tracking, and customer communication in tools such as Zendesk, Salesforce, or Jira.
Own the front door: make sure every billing, concession, and cancellation request is logged in one place, including those that arrive through Slack, email, or Gainsight, and coach CSMs and AEs on what a complete request looks like.
Act as the escalation point for the most complex, sensitive, or high-dollar cases, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension, and step in directly with customers and internal leaders when needed.
Define the handoffs, ownership, and service levels with Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal so cases stop bouncing between teams.
Set the standards for how the team separates a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and how concession and cancellation exceptions are sized, documented, and routed through the approval matrix.
Build the metrics and reporting for the function, including volume, days to resolution, repeat errors, concession dollars, and renewal risk tied to billing issues, and use them to manage the team and show impact.
Fix repeat causes: own the root-cause tagging on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved, such as segment-move bugs, term rounding, and AE handoff gaps.
Partner with Support, Finance, Sales Ops, and Product on billing improvement work, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.
Use AI to improve how the team works, from structuring case timelines to drafting summaries, while keeping approvals, amounts, and root-cause conclusions with people.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.
Minimum requirements for the role:
7+ years of experience in sales operations, deal desk, contracts, billing operations, order to cash, revenue operations, or a similar finance and operations role.

title: Electrical Engineering Manager (Onsite)
description:
ABOUT STANDARD BOTS

At Standard Bots, we're revolutionizing real-world automation by making robotic systems accessible to everyone. Our AI-powered platform enables robots to tackle unprecedented challenges through an intuitive instruction interface, bringing the power of software automation to physical spaces.

What you'll do:

We're looking for an Electrical Engineering Manager to lead the team that owns the electronics at the heart of our robots: motor controllers, power distribution, compute, camera, battery management, and sensing boards. You will be accountable for the technical output of the entire electrical engineering team: the quality, schedule, and manufacturability of every board we design and release. You'll stay hands-on in design and in the lab, report to our Head of Hardware, and partner with Mechanical, Software, Functional Safety, and Manufacturing to ship hardware that is simple, reliable, and manufacturable at scale.

📍 Location

This is an on-site role based at our Glen Cove, NY factory, where our robots are designed, built, and tested. On-site, you'll have a fully equipped electronics lab, production robots, and our manufacturing floor steps from your desk.

Responsibilities

Lead the team

 - Lead, hire, and grow the electrical engineering team: set clear goals, run 1:1s and performance reviews, and build a team where strong engineers do their best work

 - Delegate effectively: match work to each engineer's strengths and growth, give clear ownership, and stay close enough to catch problems early without becoming the bottleneck

 - Own the technical output of the team: plan and prioritize electrical work across programs, assign owners, track schedules, and hold the quality bar so every board that leaves the team is reviewed, tested, and ready for production

 - Scope and estimate electrical work with hardware leadership, flag technical and schedule risks early, and make clear trade-offs between scope, schedule, and resources

 - Put in place the right amount of process to keep the team fast and the engineering sound: design reviews, the component library, the release process, design checklists, and test standards, in partnership with the team's technical leads. Enough process to ensure good outcomes, never so much that it slows the team down

 - Work closely with the mechanical engineering team as one hardware team: co-own the electrical-mechanical interfaces (packaging, thermal, cabling, connectors), plan builds together, and solve integration problems side by side

 - Represent electrical engineering in cross-functional decisions with Software, Functional Safety, Manufacturing, and Product, and drive those decisions to closure

 - Mentor early-career engineers: teach good design and debug habits through reviews and time in the lab, and advise associate, mid-level, and senior engineers on technical and personal advancement

Stay hands-on

 - Spend roughly 75% of your time on hands-on engineering for the first few months: schematic capture, PCB layout (including high-current power and high-speed digital), board bring-up, test plans, and root-cause debugging in the lab on our most critical boards. As the team grows, there will still be a lot of technical review but individual design work will drop to 25% or less over time as the team grows, however you will stay deeply involved in the technical decisions and work of the team

 - Drive key architecture and component decisions through conceptual design, requirements definition, and trade studies, and advise hardware leadership on technical strategy

 - Own the relationship with PCB fabrication and assembly vendors; drive DFM/DFA feedback into designs, and support production issues

Who you are

We don't require a background in robotics, but we do require deep, hands-on electronics experience and a track record of leading engineers.

We're looking for leaders who are self-driven, optimistic, creative, resourceful, and highly collaborative. We have no requirement for a background in robotics, but find most success with engineers excited by the domain and looking to apply deep electronics expertise (from motor drives, power electronics, embedded compute, automotive, or aerospace) to robots they can watch move.

Skills you'll bring:

 - Experience: You have a bachelor's or graduate degree in Electrical Engineering (or a related field), 15+ years designing, building, and testing PCBAs, including designs you've taken through production release, and 7+ years leading and managing electrical engineers

 - Leadership: You have hired, coached, and grown engineers, including early-career engineers; you set clear priorities, give direct feedback, and hold a high technical bar

 - Delegation: You delegate well: you give engineers real ownership, trust them with it, and step in only where your help changes the outcome

 - Right-sized Process: You know how much process a fast-moving hardware team needs, and you add it only where it improves speed or engineering outcomes

 - Cross-team Communication: You have a very strong ability to communicate with other teams and departments across the company (Software, Functional Safety, Manufacturing, Product, and leadership): you explain electrical trade-offs in terms each team understands, share plans, status, and risks early, and build the trust that lets cross-team decisions happen quickly

 - Collaboration: You are very collaborative across the company; you work as one team with mechanical engineers, and you treat the electrical-mechanical interface as a shared problem, not a handoff. Ability to collaborate with Production, Operations, Procurement, Quality, Customer support, etc. will be key to success in this role. 

 - Ownership of Output: You plan and deliver a team's work against real schedules, catch problems in review before they reach the lab or the factory, and take responsibility for what your team ships

 - EE Depth: You have mastery of power electronics (motor drivers and inverter stages, switch-mode supplies, power sequencing and protection), digital electronics (MCUs, FPGAs, Ethernet, USB, SPI/I2C/UART, signal-integrity fundamentals), and analog electronics (op-amps, filters, ADC/DAC signal chains, precision sensing)

 - Tool Fluency: You're proficient in Altium Designer (or similar EDA tools) for schematic capture and multi-layer layout, including constraint-driven routing for high-speed and high-current designs

 - Debugging Mastery: You know how to attack a hardware problem with a scope, logic/protocol analyzer, and bench instruments, document what you find, and converge on a fix quickly, and you teach your team to do the same

 - Clarity of Communication: You excel in written and verbal communication: clear design documentation, crisp trade studies, and design reviews that make your team better

 - Impact Driven: You relentlessly seek user impact and value execution over technical idealism; a reliable, manufacturable board that ships beats an elegant one that never leaves the lab

 - Proactive Simplicity: You prioritize simplicity, reliability, and velocity, and proactively identify opportunities to improve proposed designs or incumbent hardware

 - Growth + Optimism: You are excited by new domains and challenges, and eager to pick up new context to accelerate your impact

 - Excelling in Ambitious Environments: You excel in dynamic and ambitious environments, working with a diverse group of individuals and backgrounds

Bonus points for:

 - Building or scaling an electrical engineering team at a hardware startup, including setting up design standards, release processes, and lab infrastructure

 - Leading engineers across more than one site or program at the same time

 - High-speed design (PCIe Gen1–5, USB3/4, MIPI, GMSL, 10G Ethernet) with high-current power delivery for compute modules, and a working understanding of signal and power integrity (impedance control, crosstalk, PDN) and how to mitigate issues

 - Camera electronics and image sensor integration (MIPI, GMSL, sensor power and clocking)

 - Dense or space-constrained boards (HDI, flex, rigid-flex) and their fabrication trade-offs

 - Motor electromagnetic design and motor control (FOC, current sensing, encoder interfaces), or control systems for robotic manipulation or locomotion

 - Familiarity with embedded programming of DSPs, MCUs, and FPGAs; LTspice and Python for simulation, analysis, and test automation

 - EMC/EMI design and regulatory compliance testing (CE/UL, IEC 61000 series), including pre-compliance debugging

 - Real-time industrial fieldbuses (EtherCAT, CAN/CANopen, EtherNet/IP) and safety-rated electronics to ISO 13849 or IEC 61508 (redundant architectures, STO, safety fieldbus)

 - Taking products from prototype through NPI to volume manufacturing: DFM/DFT, test fixtures, yield improvement

Compensation and Benefits:

The base salary range for this role is $180,000 to $230,000, depending on experience. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Core Connectivity
description:
Zoox is building the world's most advanced self-driving hardware and software solution, and nearly every part of it depends on moving data reliably. Sensor frames to perception, planner decisions to vehicle controls, telemetry to the cloud, and remote operator video back down again. All of it crosses process, host, and network boundaries under hard latency and reliability budgets, on a vehicle that has to keep working when a link degrades or a network gets congested. The Software Core Connectivity team owns that data path end to end: in-vehicle messaging (pub/sub, RPC, inter-process and inter-host transport), the vehicle's internal network, and vehicle-to-cloud connectivity. It also owns the transport and serialization abstractions the rest of the software organization builds on. Every one of those paths crosses a team boundary, so the work happens alongside firmware, product security, simulation, manufacturing, and IT, and those partners rely on this team for transport and networking depth to achieve their goals. As the team leader you will own the roadmap and the release commitments, and you will spend a real share of your time in those partnerships. In this role, you will:

  • Design and build low-latency inter-process and inter-host transport in C++: zero-copy data paths, shared-memory buffers, and lock-free queues. Measure and drive down end-to-end latency and jitter as message volume grows.

  • Make the transport hold up when processes crash or restart, hosts start out of order, and networks drop or delay packets. Chase fleet and simulation issues to root cause and fix them in the design.

  • Build the pub/sub and RPC messaging APIs application teams build on, so they get the delivery, ordering, and latency guarantees they need without having to understand the transport underneath.

  • Evolve message schemas and the Protocol Buffers based serialization layer: schema evolution, compact encodings, and moving existing users onto new formats without breaking anyone.

  • Set technical direction for a part of the stack and lead designs that span several teams.

    • Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in computer science, electrical / computer engineering, or equivalent experience, and 7+ years of experience in software development.

  • Strong modern C++ on Linux, in large codebases with performance-critical paths.

  • A background in transport or networking software, such as messaging systems, network protocols, or communication between distributed systems.

  • Experience building low-latency systems, and a track record of measuring and reducing tail latency, using techniques such as zero-copy, shared memory, lock-free data structures, and cache-aware data layout.

  • Solid systems fundamentals: concurrency, memory management, process lifecycle, sockets and the Linux networking stack.

  • Experience with PTP (IEEE 1588) or other time synchronization across machines, or with UDP multicast, MTU and fragmentation behavior, or time-sensitive networking.
